what_its_for: Penicillin G Benzathine is an antibiotic used to treat and prevent certain bacterial infections. It is commonly used to treat strep throat, syphilis, and other infections caused by bacteria that are sensitive to penicillin. It is also used to prevent rheumatic fever from coming back in people who have had it before.
how_to_take: This medication is given as a shot (injection) into a muscle, usually in the buttocks or thigh. It is always given by a healthcare provider such as a nurse or doctor in a clinic or hospital setting. You will never inject this medication yourself at home. It is very important that this medicine is NEVER given into a vein (IV), as this can cause serious, life-threatening reactions. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you feel severe pain, numbness, or notice skin color changes at the injection site.
dosing: Your dose will depend on the type of infection being treated, your age, and your weight. For strep throat in adults and children over 27 kg (60 lbs), the usual dose is a single injection of 1.2 million units. For syphilis, dosing varies based on the stage of the disease and may require multiple injections spaced one week apart. For prevention of rheumatic fever, injections are typically given every 3 to 4 weeks on an ongoing basis. Always follow the schedule your doctor gives you. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a scheduled injection appointment, call your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not skip doses, especially if you are using this medicine to prevent rheumatic fever or to treat syphilis, as missing doses can allow the infection to return or worsen. Do not try to double up on doses.
storage: This medication is stored and handled only by your healthcare provider or pharmacy. It must be kept refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). It should never be frozen. The medication should be protected from light. If you notice any unusual particles or color changes in the medication, your healthcare provider should not use it.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about ALL medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before receiving this injection. Avoid taking other antibiotics at the same time unless your doctor specifically tells you to. If you are taking blood thinners such as warfarin (Coumadin), let your doctor know because penicillin may affect how well your blood clots. Avoid probenecid unless your doctor prescribes it, as it can increase the level of penicillin in your blood. Do not drink alcohol excessively while being treated for a serious infection, as it can slow your recovery.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency medical help RIGHT AWAY if you experience any of the following after your injection: difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe skin rash or hives, dizziness or fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe pain, skin turning blue or white, or loss of feeling at or near the injection site, seizures, confusion, or severe headache, severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody (which could be a sign of a serious gut infection called C. diff), yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), or dark urine. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not start improving within a few days or if they get worse.
when_it_works: Because Penicillin G Benzathine is a long-acting antibiotic, it releases slowly into your body over days to weeks after a single injection. You may start to feel better within 1 to 3 days for infections like strep throat, but the medicine continues working in your body for up to 4 weeks. For syphilis, improvement may take longer and will be monitored with follow-up blood tests. Even if you feel better, it is important to complete any additional scheduled injections your doctor has ordered.
special_populations: Children: This medication can be used in children but the dose is adjusted based on weight. Injections in infants and young children should be given with extra care to avoid nerve or blood vessel injury. Pregnancy: Penicillin G Benzathine is generally considered safe to use during pregnancy and is actually the recommended treatment for syphilis in pregnant women to protect both the mother and baby. Always tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of penicillin may pass into breast milk. This is generally considered safe, but let your doctor know if you are breastfeeding, especially if your baby has any allergies. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may need to monitor you more closely or adjust your treatment schedule. Allergies: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin, amoxicillin, ampicillin, or any other antibiotic, especially cephalosporins, before receiving this injection.
